newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Scitex estimated Q4 share loss $0.49.
newsitem.headline: Scitex estimated Q4 share loss $0.49.

text.p: Lehman Brothers said it expected Israel's Scitex Corp to show continued losses in fourth-quarter 1996 and first-quarter 1997, but that it would return to profitability in the final quarter of next year.

Analyst Theodor Kundtz said he expected the company, a maker of electronic pre-press, digital printing and digital video equipment, to show a loss of $0.49 a share in the fourth quarter and $0.35 in first-quarter 1997.
By third-quarter 1997 Scitex should be breaking even and in the fourth show modest earnings of $0.18 per share.

Last week Scitex reported a $151 million loss, equal to $3.53 a share, in large part due to write downs and restructuring costs in its flagging electornic pre-press business, which is concentrated in its graphic arts division.

"We are expecting the graphics arts business to show sequential improvement in the fourth quarter, although sales are likely to be below year-earlier levels," Kundtz said. "For 1997, we assume a more modest decline in graphic arts equipment sales -- around 11 percent to $257 million."

Kundtz noted that Scitex's other businesses were performing well. He said Scitex Digital Video, a new business, should begin breaking even in the fourth quarter and show a 44 percent rise in revenues next year to $100 million.

Kundtz said "back of the envelope" valuations of the digital printing and video divisions plus cash equalled Scitex's current market capitalization. "Thus zero value (is) being assigned to the core graphic arts business," Kundtz concluded.
As a result, he confirmed Scitex's 2 value rating.
